clue.text: Tough, one novel Sandy's penned?

indicators.note: what is penned is written inside or shut in a pen, so these letters go within others

parts.note: the first and last letters of the name stand for its owner
the Roman numeral for one
novel as an adjective means new

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a novel written by Sandy is a tough read.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul takes just the outside of the name, with nothing but the possessive to tell you so; sinewy is the stringy quality of tough meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinewy meat or a sinewy person is stringy and muscular, so it is a fair synonym for tough.

clue.text: Drink spiked by staff — sabotage

indicators.note: a drink that is spiked has something slipped into it, so the other word goes inside

parts.note: to sup is to drink
a crew is the staff of a ship or plane

explanation.surface: A worker's drink has been tampered with by colleagues as an act of sabotage.
explanation.definitionFit: To screw up a plan is to ruin it, which is what sabotage does deliberately.

clue.text: See 19 Across
Flesh from the ocean offered 24 in old song, loosely speaking?

indicators.note: speaking says the words are heard, and loosely admits the match is only approximate

parts.note: the entry at 24 is the last word of the wartime song title We'll Meet Again

explanation.surface: A nostalgic quip that the old Vera Lynn song was secretly about eating whale.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 Across is AGAIN, so the song is We'll Meet Again; said lazily, its first two words become this answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Whale meat is the edible flesh of a whale, a sea creature, so it is flesh from the ocean.

clue.text: Millionaire briefly plying rich man with lagers

indicators.note: plying someone with drink gets them tipsy, and these words stagger into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who briefly had a fortune keeps buying a wealthy man beers.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Ingram is the army major who won the top prize on the TV quiz Who Wants to Be a Millionaire? in 2001, then lost it when convicted of cheating with coughs.
explanation.definitionFit: He held the million-pound prize only until the cheating verdict, so he was a millionaire for a short time.

clue.text: Noise after composer of noteless music shut up

indicators.note: after places the noise second, behind the composer in the finished word

parts.note: John Cage wrote 4'33", a piece in which no notes are played
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: Silence finally falls once the avant-garde composer is told to stop the racket.
explanation.walkthrough: John Cage's 4'33" is famously four and a half minutes of a performer playing nothing, hence noteless music.
explanation.definitionFit: To be shut up is to be confined, and something caged in is enclosed and unable to leave.

clue.text: Turn seat, lifting lid

indicators.note: lifting off a lid takes away the top, so the first letter of the word comes off

parts.note: a saddle is the seat on a horse or bicycle

explanation.surface: Instructions for flipping a toilet seat over while raising its lid.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the first letter is the top, so the lid is the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs that addle go rotten, just as milk is said to turn when it goes off.

clue.text: Lay down rules where supporter is delayed

parts.note: a leg supports a table or chair
taken as written
something delayed arrives late

explanation.surface: A complaint that rules get made when a fan is held up.
explanation.definitionFit: To legislate is to make laws, which is to lay down the rules people must follow.

clue.text: Poser: one surely won't be missed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who poses for a painter or photographer
second meaning: in sport, an easy chance that should certainly be taken

explanation.walkthrough: 'Poser' looks like a puzzle, but here it is the person who poses.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitter is an artist's model, and also a catch or shot so easy that failing it is a disgrace.

clue.text: Goody-goody above naughty crime

parts.note: pi is short for pious, a self-righteous goody-goody
racy means risqué or mildly naughty

explanation.surface: A prig sits on top of a wrongdoer, as if moral rank were physical position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'above' places one piece over the other in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Piracy, robbery at sea or illegal copying, is a criminal offence.

clue.text: London borough behind minister's brief

indicators.note: behind puts the borough after the minister's title in the finished word

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a church minister's title
Ealing is a borough in west London

explanation.surface: A borough sits in the shadow of a government minister's portfolio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' looks like a minister's area of responsibility, but it is an adjective for skimpy clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief skirt or swimsuit shows a lot of skin, so it is revealing.

clue.text: Say what to do to get that whole number?

indicators.note: Say asks for the following word to be heard rather than read, changing its spelling

parts.words: what to do to get that whole
parts.note: heard aloud the phrase asks how to make a pit, and the answer is the two-word instruction to excavate it

explanation.surface: A maths pupil asks how to arrive at an integer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whole number' looks like the definition, an integer, but 'Say' turns 'whole' into a hole, which you dig; only 'number' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A digit is one of the numerals 0 to 9, each of them a number in its own right.

clue.text: Aggravated, son donned trousers

indicators.note: used as a verb, to trouser something is to pocket it, so one piece is tucked inside another

parts.note: donned clothes are worn
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A cross boy grudgingly pulled on his trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' looks like the garment the son put on, but it is a verb meaning pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: Something aggravated has been made more serious, that is, made worse.

clue.text: A flower adorning garment for recipient

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a decoration adorning something wraps around it, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river, here the Dee
a dress is a garment

explanation.surface: A bloom pinned to a frock makes a gift for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is crossword shorthand for a river, as it flows; the Dee runs through Wales and England.
explanation.definitionFit: An addressee is the person a letter or parcel is sent to, its recipient.

clue.text: Hot shower steamy, ultimately

parts.note: to pepper is to shower, as with shot or questions

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A hot shower ends up filling the bathroom with steam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shower' looks like a noun in the bathroom but works as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Peppery food is spicy, which is hot in the sense of fiery on the tongue.

clue.text: Top career excited father

indicators.note: something excited is stirred up and agitated, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man thrilled by his brilliant career becomes a dad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'father' is a verb here, not the noun it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: To father a child is to beget it, and to procreate is to produce offspring.

clue.text: Dead ant less filling, one feeds on termites

indicators.note: without its filling means the middle of the word is emptied out

parts.note: a dead limb has no feeling, it is numb
taken as written

explanation.surface: An insect lies dead and hollowed out, eaten by something that preys on termites.
explanation.walkthrough: The ant loses its middle letter. The numbat is a small striped Australian marsupial.
explanation.definitionFit: The numbat, or banded anteater, lives almost entirely on termites, so it is one that feeds on them.

clue.text: Ray secures lid on new cocktail

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so one piece is gripped inside another

parts.note: the manta is a large ray
lid is slang for a hat
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A bartender called Ray fixes the top onto a freshly made drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' looks like a man's name but is the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A Manhattan is a cocktail of whiskey and sweet vermouth, named after the New York borough.

clue.text: Black article scraped off back of sofa bed

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: scraped off the back means removed from the end of the following word

parts.note: an ottoman is a low upholstered seat
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone cleans a black mark off the back of a sofa bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sofa bed' reads as one item of furniture; it splits, with 'bed' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The bottom of the sea or of a river is its bed, the ground at the lowest point.

clue.text: Sweet thing in pub with poisonous atmosphere?

parts.note: the red planet's thin carbon dioxide air could not be breathed
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: A bar so smoky its air is toxic serves a sweet treat.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a whimsical picture: a pub on another planet. A Mars bar is a British chocolate bar of nougat and caramel.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mars bar is a chocolate confection, a sweet in British usage, so a sweet thing.

clue.text: Dalliance in essence over, Andrew? I don't believe it!

indicators.note: dalliance is toying or playing about with something, so the words played with are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is astonished that Andrew's affair has basically ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dalliance' looks like the subject of the gossip, but it is the signal that the next three words are to be played with.
explanation.definitionFit: Wonders never cease is an idiom said, often ironically, when surprised, just like exclaiming that you cannot believe it.

clue.text: Obtain and taste bitter

parts.note: to win something is to obtain it
to try food is to taste it

explanation.surface: Someone gets hold of a drink, samples it, and finds it bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bitter' wants to be a flavour after 'taste', but here it describes the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitter weather is piercingly cold, which is what wintry weather is.

clue.text: According to Spooner, cake layer light

indicators.note: William Spooner was famed for swapping the starting sounds of words, so the initial sounds here change places

parts.note: a bun is a small cake and a seam is a layer, as of coal; swapping their first sounds gives the answer

explanation.surface: Spooner describes the light, airy tier of a sponge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' sounds like an adjective describing the cake, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunbeam is a ray of sunshine, a shaft of light.

clue.text: Small nails — a lot

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothes labels
tacks are small nails

explanation.surface: Someone buying small nails finds the shop has plenty.
explanation.definitionFit: Stacks is informal for a large quantity, as in stacks of money, meaning a lot.

clue.text: Club in there, or bats

indicators.note: bats is slang for crazy, so the preceding letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Is the club stocked with sports bats, or only with something else?
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' looks like cricket or baseball bats, fitting 'Club', but it is the adjective meaning mad.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-iron is a golf club with a fairly straight-faced iron head.

clue.text: Powerful people announcing the score of the Roman Empire?

indicators.note: announcing something means saying it out loud, so the letters are heard rather than read

parts.words: the score of the Roman Empire
parts.note: a score is twenty, which the Romans wrote as two Xs

explanation.surface: Grandees proclaim the Roman Empire's final tally, as if after a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' looks like a match result but is the old word for twenty; say the Roman numeral's two letters and you hear the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Execs, short for executives, are senior managers who hold the power in a company.

clue.text: Encore: a band not entirely welcoming one

indicators.note: welcoming a guest means taking them inside, so one piece goes within the other
not entirely means falling short of the whole, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
a gang is a band of people
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A band calls for an encore but does not fully welcome a soloist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' suggests musicians, matching 'Encore', but it means a group of people.
explanation.definitionFit: Encore is French for again, and an audience shouting it wants a piece played once more.

clue.text: Slope initially dropped a shade

indicators.note: dropped at the start means the first letter of the word is lost

parts.note: a camber is the slope of a road surface

explanation.surface: A skier's slope is first lost, then appears as a coloured hue.
explanation.definitionFit: Amber is a honey-yellow colour, one shade among many.

clue.text: See 19
Where crumbs may be taken from book in story of a sentence?

definitions.text: Where crumbs may be taken from

parts.note: bird is British slang for a prison sentence, from rhyming slang bird-lime, time

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other, enclosed by it

parts.note: a tale is a story
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A reader wonders which story to borrow from a volume of prison tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sentence' looks grammatical, sitting near book and story, but it means a prison term. A bird table is a raised garden platform where food is put out for birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds peck scraps from a bird table, so it is a place where crumbs get taken.

clue.text: Old English poet meaning to cover page with rhymes, primarily

indicators.note: covering something wraps it, so the word encloses the next piece

parts.note: a word's sense is its meaning
P is the abbreviation for page

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: An Elizabethan poet intends to fill a page with verses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meaning' looks like a verb, intending, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Spenser, author of The Faerie Queene, was a sixteenth-century English poet.
